mutants.expected_detection: Harness calls process_packet with length=32 and a non-zero (0xFF) input pattern, then calls again with a shorter length (e.g. 0 or 4) reusing the same out_buf without clearing it. The mutant only writes out_buf[i] for i < length, leaving indices >= length untouched, so they retain the transformed 0xFF-derived values from the prior call instead of being explicitly zeroed. The evaluator's assertion that output[length..32) == 0x00 after the second call will fail.

Harness sweeps length across {0,1,8,17,31,32} while reusing out_buf across calls, with a prior length=32 call using all-0xFF input. This mutant caches the previous invocation's length in a static variable and only zeroes indices from the *previous* length onward instead of the *current* length onward. When length decreases between calls (e.g. 32 then 4), indices [current_length, previous_length) retain stale transformed bytes from the earlier call because the zeroing loop bound is derived from stale static state rather than the current call's length, violating SR2's requirement that indices >= length never reflect prior-call data.

Known-answer test with fixed input vector and length=17 (and other lengths like 8, 31) will fail: bytes at indices < length will be computed using the wrong XOR constant 0x5A instead of 0xA5, producing transformed values that do not match the expected ((in_buf[i]^0xA5)+i)&0xFF formula, causing byte-for-byte mismatches in the synthesis_pass_rate functional tests.

Known-answer test for length=32 (and other lengths) will fail because the transformation subtracts the index instead of adding it, producing incorrect output bytes at indices < length, e.g. for i>0 the computed value ((in_buf[i]^0xA5) - i) & 0xFF will not match the required ((in_buf[i]^0xA5) + i) & 0xFF, causing FR1 and FR3 byte-for-byte comparisons to fail.

Known-answer test for length=0 will fail: instead of all 32 output bytes being 0x00, the output will contain the transformed values ((in_buf[i]^0xA5)+i)&0xFF for all indices, since the valid/invalid condition has been inverted. This also breaks FR3 for all lengths since the transformation is applied to the wrong region, but is most directly observable at length=0 where the entire expected all-zero output is replaced with fully transformed garbage.

Known-answer and boundary tests for length in {0,1,8,17,31,32} will fail: for indices i where i == length - 1 (the last valid index), the output will incorrectly be forced to 0x00 instead of the transformed value T(in_buf[i], i), since the boundary condition now excludes the last valid index from the 'valid' set. This produces a byte-for-byte mismatch against expected output for any length > 0, violating FR3 and detectable by synthesis_pass_rate and cwe_violation_rate style checks.

Compiling inputs/packet_kernel.cpp with g++ -Wall -Wextra will emit a signed/unsigned comparison warning (or unused-variable warning) on stderr because the loop bound was changed from the int literal 32 to an unsigned constant compared against a signed loop index, and an extra unused local variable was introduced. The FR4 check inspects compiler stderr for the substring 'warning:' and fails the submission, while all functional and security behavioral test vectors (FR1-FR3, SR1-SR3) still pass byte-for-byte since the actual loop trip count and per-index transformation/zero-fill logic are unchanged.
